newsitem.title: USA: Argentine jobless rate set to fall, Fernandez says.
newsitem.headline: Argentine jobless rate set to fall, Fernandez says.

text.p: Argentina's unemployment rate looks set to fall to 15 percent in October, Economy Minister Roque Fernndez told a news conference.
"We expect to see 15 percent unemployment in October of this year," he said.
The unemployment rate last October was 17.3 percent. The government is expected to release shortly new unemployment data for May.
"The information we have indicates to us that there has been a one point drop in the unemployment rate," Fernndez said, speaking through an interpreter.
Fernndez was upbeat on Argentina's economy.
"Not only have we maintained a strong economic rebound, we have a more solid economic foundation than we could have predicted in 1996," he said.
"GDP (gross domestic product) has grown eight percent and in the second trimester of the year we will maintain this growth," the minister added.
Fernndez played down fears that the currency troubles now plaguing some Asian countries could hurt Latin America. "We don't fear any kind of impact in the region," he said.
Several Asian nations, most prominently Thailand, have recently been forced to devalue their currencies in the face of heavy selling on foreign exchange markets.

Fernndez played down concerns that Brazil might be forced to follow the lead of Asian nations and significantly devalue the real. "We don't believe Brazil will have an important significant devaluation," he said. "We think Brazil will continue with its policy of gradual change," he added.
